comments.body: I'd like to PFI [EIP-8115](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8115), [EIP-8116](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8116), and [EIP-7807](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7807) (have reduced to a non-headliner scope) for the EL side of Hegotá.

I'd like to PFI [EIP-7819](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7819).  There's already [a PR here](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11505) to merge it into the meta EIP.  The reason why 7819 is important is that, since native AA may be shipped in Hegota, it's important that the cost of deploying new smart accounts is low, but deploying accounts will actually get more expensive in Glamsterdam due to [EIP-8037](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8037).  With EIP-7819, new accounts would use simple delegate pointers instead of proxy contracts, vastly reducing the amount of new state that needs to be created, thereby reducing deployment cost.
Hi, I would like to propose [EIP-7906](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7906) for Hegotá.

I want to propose https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7668 (Remove bloom filters) for Hegotá.

Can do this very quickly: it simplifies the protocol. I also proposed it for Glamsterdam. It would work nicely together with https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8304 (Trustless log and transaction index), which explicitly does not disable bloom filters, but also notes:

> The original per-block bloom filters were moderately efficient in the beginning and now they are oversaturated and practically useless. 

Bloom filters are wasted compute, we should spend this elsewhere. Can also repurpose this header field for something else.

Hi, I would like to propose [EIP 8200](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8200) for H*

There was a talk on this a few months ago at the stateless summit: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NbYpOGU-5wU&list=PLJqWcTqh_zKF7ZR8JZNXiRzxHT2uLRMwZ&index=9 for reference !
Should we make devnet-8 the public facing network? Devnet-7 did not seem to have gotten much usage, and we've also had an issue with the faucet.
Would be good to quickly discuss the status of discv5 support in EL clients. It seem almost everyone is up-to-speed, but some small effort is still needed on Reth.

ethPandaOps would like to propose the launch of a new (short-lived) named testnet: Platåberget. (Couldn't find a metro station on Svalbard, so we had to go with a satellite station lol)

Written `plataberget` in configs and URLs, so we don't end up with two spellings floating around.

It'll have ~50k genesis validators run by us across ~50 nodes covering all CL/EL combos — but the network is fully permissionless. Anyone is welcome to join and test their validator, node, or dapp use case. We're deliberately keeping our validator set small so external validators get a real share of proposals and plenty of churn to play with.

The network launches pre-Gloas and forks to Glamsterdam 7 days after genesis, so clients go through the transition from a populated pre-fork state. Config is mainnet-faithful — only chain ID, fork versions and genesis time differ.

Exact launch date will be announced at next [ACDT](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2174) on Monday, but expect it up early August, running until at least mainnet forks Glamsterdam.

This is expected to be the last iteration and the final spec of what we ship to mainnet, unless something critical is found along the way.

I could use some core dev eyes on this [hive pr](https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1589): "clients disagree on EIP-7928 BAL contents at block 57" it's a blocker for getting rpc-compat testing working

> Would be good to quickly discuss the status of discv5 support in EL clients. It seem almost everyone is up-to-speed, but some small effort is still needed on Reth.

It seems Reth is also good on their main branch, just not on the devnet-7 branch. So let's just focus on confirming in the call.
